subject: Maths
title: Reading and writing large integers
subtitle: Place Value and Ordering Integers · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can read, write and compare large integers up to millions using place value.

key_vocab.definition: Place value tells us the value of each digit based on its position. Large numbers use thousands, millions, and billions columns.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can read, write and compare large integers up to millions using place value.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Large integers -- Place value tells us the value of each digit based on its position. Large numbers use thousands, millions, and billions columns.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Use place value columns: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten-thousands, hundred-thousands, millions.
2,456,789
2 millions, 456 thousands, 789 ones

Key examples:
  ✓ 3,500,000 = three million five hundred thousand  (reading correctly)
  ✓ 45,000 has 4 in the ten-thousands column  (place value)
  ✓ 1,000,000 = one million  (six zeros)
  ✗ 3,500,000 = thirty-five thousand  (wrong place value)
  ✗ 1,000,000 has 5 zeros  (it has 6 zeros)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – reading a large number
  Write 4,250,000 in words.
  4 is in the millions column
  250 is in the thousands
  Four million two hundred and fifty thousand
  = Four million two hundred and fifty thousand
  (Read from left to right using place value.)

Example 2 – writing in figures
  Write seven hundred and thirty-two thousand in figures.
  Seven hundred and thirty-two thousand = 732 thousand
  = 732,000
  Add three zeros for thousands
  = 732,000
  (Match each word to its place value position.)

sections.title: Writing numbers in figures
sections.content:
Write each number in figures.

(a) Sixty thousand
(b) Three hundred and forty-five thousand
(c) Two million
(d) Nine million, two hundred thousand

sections.title: Place value of digits
sections.content:
State the value of the underlined digit (shown in brackets).

(a) The 5 in 2,500,000
(b) The 3 in 4,350,000
(c) The 8 in 8,040,000
(d) The 7 in 1,070,500

sections.title: Mixed large number problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) Write 2.5 million in figures
(b) How many thousands in 3,400,000?
(c) Round 4,678,000 to the nearest million
(d) What is 100,000 more than 2,950,000?
(e) Write 850,000 in words

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 3,500,000 is three million five hundred thousand
✗ 1,000,000 has 5 zeros
✓ The 4 in 4,200,000 is worth 4 million
✗ 450,000 is bigger than 1,000,000
✓ We read large numbers from left to right
